sections.title: Prerequisite Bridge: From Discrete to Continuous
sections.content: Briefly recall histograms. Explain that as we increase data points and shrink bin widths to near zero, a bar chart transitions into a smooth curve. Introduce the shift from 'probability of a point' to 'area under the curve'.
sections.example: Visualizing a histogram of cat weights transforming into a smooth bell-shaped curve.

sections.title: Defining the PDF
sections.content: Define the PDF f(x) and its two critical properties: 1) f(x) ≥ 0 (no negative probability), and 2) The integral over the entire range must equal 1 (certainty). Emphasize that f(x) is a density, not a probability itself.
sections.example: An animation showing a 'total energy' bar filling up to exactly 100% as the area under the curve is shaded.

sections.title: The Meaning of Area
sections.content: Explain that P(a ≤ X ≤ b) is calculated as the definite integral of f(x) from a to b. Visually demonstrate this as the area between two vertical lines under the curve.
sections.example: A robot arm sensor measuring the probability of a part being within a specific tolerance range [a, b].

sections.title: The Zero-Probability Paradox
sections.content: Address the counter-intuitive fact that for continuous variables, the probability of any single exact value P(X = c) is 0. Explain this via the limit of the integral where the width approaches zero.
sections.example: A dart throwing machine aiming for a coordinate; hitting an 'exact' mathematical point has zero width, hence zero area.

sections.title: Summary & Application
sections.content: Recap: PDF gives the relative likelihood of outcomes. Final check of the properties using a simple linear function. Brief mention of how PDFs help us calculate Expected Value.
sections.example: A 'Probability Heatmap' showing where a migratory bird is most likely to be found on a flight path based on wind speed distributions.
